[times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Query times for the numbers-at-risk table. Defaults to an automatic grid. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A tidy frame with columns `strata`, `time`, and `n_risk` (one row per stratum per time point). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a stratified Kaplan-Meier estimator on the bundled `lung` dataset, then tabulate the number of subjects still at risk in each group at a chosen set of times. This returns the numbers as a tidy frame (one row per stratum and time). ::: {#c823e4c1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit a stratified Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", data=lung) # Get the numbers at risk as a tidy Polars DataFrame gw.get_risk_table_frame(km, times=[0, 250, 500, 750, 1000], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
